items.text: Dual-omics joint deconvolution, allowing reference profiles to adapt to the tumor environment and correcting for RNA contribution and cell number differences, is a testable methodological contribution.

Incorporating cell proportions as shared latent variables into the survival model and comparing with two-stage approaches can investigate the impact of measurement uncertainty and compositional constraints on prediction; this is not equivalent to treatment efficacy prediction.
Even if no clinically usable markers are obtained, R21 exploration can still deliver insights into error/identifiability, publicly available software, and cross-cancer benchmarks.

Identifiability and model misspecification: flexible cell profiles, fixed tumor purity, similar cell profiles, scale/batch differences; having more samples than cell types is not a sufficient condition.
Validation with real mixtures and strict hold-out must cover the entire joint fitting/feature and tuning pipeline, avoiding self-verification through simulation and survival information leakage.

The number of survival events, censoring/risk models, zero proportions, and tree-sequence fusion affect predictive reliability; these should be matched to the two-year exploratory scope rather than requiring immediate clinical validation.
